author: jc473
content:
There was also a couple of other subjects we’ve discussed over the last couple of day. Here’s one of the more important ones.

Fire mage mana issues. 

Currently there is a real need to go into the arcane tree with 13 points to grab Magic Absorption + Arcane Concentration. Some even like to reach for a couple of points in Arcane Meditation. All of these options feel almost mandatory to be able to have any sort of longevity with Fire during a raid. This then leaves us having to skip over talents like Improvred Fire Blast, Improved Flamestrike, Incinerate and Hotstreak (even the new buffed version) which feels quite bad.

Possible Solutions:
a) Improve Master of Elements. By doing this, you are creating further synergy with the Fire spec and the Crit stat which I think is a very intuitive solution. Fire mages naturally go for crit because of Ignite and Hotstreak, so let’s drive home this identity by having the bulk of their mana sustain tied to this stat.
So, perhaps boost Master of Elements to 20/40/60%.

b) Rearrange Arcane Talents.
You could swap the position of Arcane Focus (1st row) with Arcane Concentration (2nd row). This would allow us to get Arcane Concentration and Magic Absorption and only spending 8 points in the Arcane tree which gives us 5 more points to spend in the Fire tree.
Another version of this could be to swap Arcane Focus with Magic Absorption. This would create a typical set of options in the first row. You either complete it with 5/5 Arcane Missiles or 2/2 Arcane Subtlety + 3/3 Magic Absorption. With this rearrangement, the fire mage would only need to spend 10 points for the mana sustain talents and have 3 more to spend in the fire tree.

Hopefully you find either of these options interesting. I’d be happy for either one but I personally like improving Master of Elements more. The idea of fire mages stacking huge amounts of crit is pretty thematic to me 🙂

```
function HasIceBlock()
  local i = 1
  while true do
    local icon = UnitBuff("player", i)
    if not icon then break end
    if icon == "Interface\\Icons\\Spell_Frost_Frost" then
      return i
    end
    i = i + 1
  end
  return -1
end

function GetCooldownReady(spellName)
  local i = FindSpellIndex(spellName)
  if i then
    local start, duration, enabled = GetSpellCooldown(i, BOOKTYPE_SPELL)
    return enabled == 1 and start == 0
  end
  return false
end

function CastIceBlockOrColdSnap()
  local index = HasIceBlock()
  if index >= 1 then
    CancelPlayerBuff(index-1)
    return
  end

  local ib = "Ice Block"
  local ibcd = GetCooldownReady(ib)
  local cs = "Cold Snap"
  local cscd = GetCooldownReady(cs)

  if cscd and not ibcd then
    CastSpellByName(cs)
  elseif ibcd then
    CastSpellByName(ib) 
  end
end
```

author: Arcitec
content:
The new ignite DoT is much better. It now does the same total damage in just 4 seconds instead of 6 seconds.

In groups, the first mage owns the Ignite and all the other mages extend the 1st mage's Ignite, meaning that threat from other mages accumulates on the mage that owns the stack of Ignite.

So the change to 4 second duration means each mage has more chance that the stack has fallen off and that the new stack becomes owned by them, so that they get counted as damage source and get some threat.

Edit: Apparently the threat problem has been improved so that threat is shared between every mage that contributed to the stack.

Anyway, here is what Turtle wrote in 1.18 patch notes. I am guessing they are referring to the fact that a 6 second duration never really falls off if you have many fire mages in the raid, meaning that after it has hit 5 stacks, the extra mages don't contribute Ignite at all. So a shorter duration lets the stack fall off periodically and rotate between the raiders.

> Ignite: Duration reduced from 6 seconds to 4 seconds.
> 
> Developer Comment: We're reverting the original duration for Ignite due to the longer duration not fully hitting its mark, having the effect of having more Fire Mages end up as a throughput loss compared to only having one and the solo Fire Mage being forced to spam Scorch to reliably keep up the Ignite.
> 
> Initially this was modified to a 6 second duration to free up Mages to play different specs while being able to keep Ignite up with fewer Fire Mages. Now with the other specs being attractive enough to play on their own we once again want to promote more Ignite cooperation.
> 
> We'll keep monitoring Ignite even after this change as it's a delicate talent with a unique mechanic.

author: Luden TA
content: If you get nampower(client mod) and nampower settings(addon) there is a setting where you can double tap spells to interrupt your missiles after the next tick of the missiles so that you don’t clip a missile. If you don’t know what clipping a missile is it means you are channeling and then cancelling your missiles before the next missile comes out thus you are channeling extra time for no reason. For rupture any time you do not have the rupture debuff you will want to cancel your missiles to cast rupture. If you get a temporary convergence proc and still have rupture debuff wait until it falls off to cast rupture even if that means you channel for 2 missiles then cancel for rupture(assuming you have the mana to be that aggressive with canceling missiles.) as for surge you want to interrupt missiles for it any time you have less than 25 percent haste I believe. That breakpoint may be a little less but pretty much if you have AP or MQG popped don’t interrupt for surge. If you have rupture debuff you can hold off on pressing surge for a couple seconds so that you aren’t wasting rupture debuff but don’t wait too long or surge will no longer be available. Also it has a cd so using it sooner means it will be available again sooner.

content:
I don't really know and care that much about gearing in lower tiers, it's quite possible that different stats are a bit better than others there, but you have to understand that stats don't work in a vacuum, they will weights differently depending of your other stats. It also should be noted that they can be quite different depending of the fight length, for example with my gear, it's something like the following:
30s: crit 13.18 SP, haste 13 SP
1 minute: crit 13.3 SP, haste 14.32 SP
3 minutes: crit 13.09 SP, haste 16.27 SP
And if using AP/MQG separately on longer fight:
1 minute: crit 13.31 SP, haste 15.68 SP
3 minutes: crit 13.18 SP, haste 17 SP
Note that this is haste applied multiplicatively to my current gear, if inputting on a planner like this one, it should be downscaled to one "raw" haste, meaning you should divide those haste weights by 1.0825.

author: Izzo
content:
It's not 4,7% haste. Haste works multiplicatively, so when all your stuff procs: tbos 1,05. * whip 1,03 * talents 1,05 * gear 1,01^8 (rough estimate) * AP 1,30 * 5t3 1,05 = ~167% castspeed. Casttime will be around 60% of base. 
In that case the 5% haste from the set will effectively give around 7%P castspeed. 
The set has a good uptime and only gets better with buffs and better gear (more haste/crit).
It's a great setboni that you usually drop only when you get a good number of T3 pieces.
